Bug_Details:
The likely intention of a user calling Thread.run() is to start the execution of code within a new thread. This, however, is not what
happens when this method is called.
The purpose of Thread.run() is to provide a method that users can overwrite to specify the code to be executed. The actual thread is
then started by calling Thread.start() . When Thread.run() is called directly, it will be executed as a regular method within
the current thread.
Bug_Explanation: The run method of the Thread class is called directly and not via start method. This is the exact problem described in the bug rule. The 'run()' method is not a separate thread but rather the method to be executed by a new thread, whose start is usually invoked.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the `showBug` method which in turn calls `myThread.run()` which directly calls the `run` method of the `Thread` class. This violates the rule 'Thread.run() should not be called directly'. The test case is designed to fail due to this bug.
